EXEMPTION OF WILLIAM S. GARLAND FROM CoMPULSORY RETIREMENT
FoR AGE

WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that William S. Garland,
civil engineer, Bureau of Aeronautics, Navy Department, who, during the month of
January, 1939, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation
from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for
age for a period of one year:

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in
me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S. C., title 5,
sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said William S. Garland from compulsory retirement
for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1940.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT
THe Waite Hovsz,

October 28, 1988.

[No 7995]

U.S. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE: 1938

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 7995 of October 28, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt, exempts William S. Garland from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1940, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). The held text is the American Presidency Project web transcription (APP node 210566, Common Crawl capture 2026-01-16T02:40:31Z); its page record in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names Executive Order 7995, the date agrees with the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file. The order is one whereas paragraph and one operative paragraph, so it is one clause. The exemption ends by its own terms on January 31, 1940; per research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md that day is recorded as the inclusive end, and the exclusive reading (the exemption stops when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The packet records later extension order(s) No. 8326 (January 22, 1940); each is entered as a later event, and the machine search hits for this order (OFR catalog and held-text name search) are exactly those order(s).

Garland from service before January 31, 1940 would be a fact about the person rather than an act on the order and is not shown by any held source.","independent_command_check":"The order contains no independent continuing command: it creates no report, regulation or duty, and the statute it cites is its authority, not a command of the order.","savings_check":"Savings are a fixed-period permission with no continuing consequence stated in the order or any held source; recorded as accrued during the period.","scope_check":"The order names one person and has a single operative paragraph (the first paragraph only recites the finding of public interest). One clause covers the whole order; the clause span in the dossier is the full text from the whereas paragraph through the signature block."}
